method.method_draft: Use a geometric construction/vector-rotation view. From the image, note that A is on the first-quadrant branch of the inverse-proportion graph and C is the point on the positive x-axis with x-coordinate 4, twice the x-coordinate of A. From the text, A=(2,4), so on the inverse-proportion curve xy is constant: xy=8. Therefore when x=4, the corresponding point of the curve has y=8/4=2; the required point D, vertically above C because CD is a side of the square and CM lies on the x-axis, is D=(4,2). Now the side vector from C to D is (0,2). A square can be built on either side of this vertical side; rotating (0,2) by ±90° gives the possible vectors from C to M: (-2,0) or (2,0). Therefore M=C+(-2,0)=(2,0) or M=C+(2,0)=(6,0).

So the coordinates of M are (2,0) or (6,0).
